label: sec:algebraic-substrate-preamble
html:
We exhibit the algebraic object whose internal geometry generates the physical observations. The quantum vacuum formalises as a self-dual Frobenius--Hopf algebra A living in a rigid monoidal category \mathbf{C}.

The algebra A carries three layers of structure. The Frobenius form \lambda \colon A \to \mathbf{1} and the Hopf comultiplication \Delta \colon A \to A \otimes A endow A with an inner product and a coalgebra structure, related by the Frobenius compatibility condition. A categorical Reeb derivation \xi_q \colon A \to A encodes the observer drift—the intrinsic time evolution generated by the contact structure on the state bundle \mathcal{S}. The spectral geometry of Bring's curve \mathcal{B} provides the coordinate fibers: the 2g = 8 independent cycles of this genus-4 curve determine the fundamental modes of the Reeb spectrum.

Self-duality is the principle that closes the construction. The rigid dualizing complex \omega_A^\bullet forms the duality theory for the non-commutative algebra A. The Frobenius form induces a quasi-isomorphism A \xrightarrow{\sim} \omega_A^\bullet, establishing that the observer trace \Phi = \lambda \circ \mu and the observed state space are intrinsically paired. The substrate is simultaneously the algebra of observables and the space on which those observables act.
